start_record.expected_result: Reduce avoidable initial blank-screen time and restore one bounded real-account model request through the deployed Tailnet website.

observations.scope_boundary: This task diagnoses and repairs page startup and a single-account model request. It does not add or switch accounts, test quota failover, or claim cross-account continuity.
observations.result: M6.8 passed. The standalone 8215 site stayed active, while an isolated 8216 codex-web integration completed one authorized model request through the router, reduced avoidable startup delays, preserved login across routed service restarts, and passed bounded pre/post-semantic failure tests.

residual_risks: Every Tailnet device allowed to reach port 8214 will receive the same high-privilege real account and workspace access.
Every Tailnet device allowed to reach port 8215 can operate the standalone codex service user and consume the configured real account.
The direct HTTP compatibility fallback is not cryptographically secure; prefer a Tailscale HTTPS origin.
The real account login can expire or be revoked and must then be authorized again.
The upstream Linux terminal native module was not qualified.
Only one usable real account is configured, so a real A-to-B switch is not qualified.
Cross-account continuity remains unverified; switching starts a new backend session.
